group_assessment.weighting: The Harvard/Brigham Advanced Parkinson Research centre with a large international longitudinal consortium. Strong on survival genetics; no WWOX biology. This is the discovery source of the WWOX PD-progression SNP that wave 6 met second-hand in PMID 42135313.

resolved.how: Reference 49 (Mallaret 2014, SCAR12) is the paper's only WWOX-direct citation; LEGEND holds it in the corpus and in its registries, and it is cited here only to say what WWOX mutation causes.

entries.proposition: The authors class the WWOX result as suggestive, not as a discovered locus.
entries.snippet: Two suggestive association signals were located in Transmembrane Protein 108 (TMEM108; NC_000003.11:g.132985956A>C) and WW Domain Containing Oxidoreductase (WWOX; NC_000016.9:g.78281160A>G) loci, respectively

entries.proposition: Genome-wide significance for WWOX is reached only in the combined discovery-plus-replication analysis; discovery alone is suggestive and replication alone is p<0.05.
entries.snippet: These loci achieved genome-wide significance (P < 5 × 10−8) in the combined analysis of discovery and replication populations with suggestive P < 5 × 10−5 in discovery and P < 0.05 in the replication cohort

entries.proposition: The WWOX exposure is one imputed common variant, rs8050111, risk allele G, frequency 0.066, HR 2.12 (1.63-2.75), discovery p 1.08E-06, replication p 0.01, combined p 2.37E-08.
The longitudinal cognitive-decline support for WWOX is a mixed-model p of 0.009.
entries.snippet: Patients carrying the WWOX variant had a more rapid longitudinal cognitive decline in MMSE scores compared to non-carriers with P = 0.009 in the LMM analysis

entries.proposition: The figure that supports the WWOX survival claim uses a different genetic coding from Table 1, and its p values are uncorrected for multiple testing — the authors say so themselves.
entries.snippet: the HR and P values shown here for TMEM108 rs138073281 and WWOX rs8050111 are different from the HR and P values from the main analysis

entries.proposition: The paper states that WWOX, like the other two loci, is expressed specifically in dopamine and pyramidal neurons.
entries.snippet: TMEM108 and WWOX are both expressed in human brain (Extended Data Fig. 4) and specifically in dopamine and pyramidal neurons

entries.proposition: The panel cited for that sentence shows the opposite for WWOX: its laser-capture expression is as high in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and fibroblasts as in the two neuron classes, so the word 'specifically' holds for RIMS2 and TMEM108 and not for WWOX.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Extended Data Fig. 5 (nihms-1684407-f0008.jpg), three panels on a shared log10(FPKM+0.01) axis over SNDA (n = 86), MCPY (n = 3), TCPY (n = 10), PBMC (n = 4) and FB (n = 3). RIMS2: neuron medians about 1.5-1.7 against PBMC about -1.9. TMEM108: neuron medians about 0.3-0.65 against PBMC about -1.0 and FB about -0.9. WWOX: SNDA about 0.35, MCPY about 0.2, TCPY about 0.1, PBMC about 0.5 and FB about 0.35 — the two non-neural classes sit at or above the neuronal medians.
entries.contradicts_needle: specifically in dopamine and pyramidal neurons

entries.proposition: The paper's only statement about what WWOX does is a one-clause citation of the SCAR12 primary; it carries no WWOX mechanism of its own.
entries.snippet: WWOX is mutated in autosomal recessive ataxia with mental retardation and epilepsy

entries.proposition: rs8050111 is imputed, not directly genotyped, with an imputation R2 of 0.961 and a 98.9 per cent concordance check.
entries.snippet: Imputation average call rates (AvgCall) and imputation R2 values were for rs182987047, 0.998 and 0.98, respectively; for rs138073281, 0.996 and 0.888; for rs8050111, 0.997 and 0.961.

entries.found_or_sought: sought - question: does the supplement carry a WWOX-locus datum the main text does not

entries.proposition: Supplementary Table 3 carries a SECOND WWOX-region variant, rs142789964 (chr16 78.52 Mb, hg19; risk allele T, frequency 0.014; HR 3.49, 95% CI 2.25-5.42; discovery P 2.72e-8, replication P 0.59, combined P 1.95e-6; nearest gene WWOX), distinct from the main-text rs8050111 (chr16 78.28 Mb; HR 2.12; discovery 1.08e-6, replication 0.01, combined 2.37e-8). The genome-wide-significant discovery variant does not replicate (P 0.59); the variant that replicates weakly (P 0.01) did not reach genome-wide significance in discovery. 'The WWOX locus' therefore names two signals about 240 kb apart with opposite discovery/replication profiles; neither is a coding or loss-of-function variant, and the nearest-gene label is positional.
